claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the model for launch is compliant and evidentially supported on the current record despite a 1.3-point miss in the grant compliance review segment and an open disclosure/materiality question.

concern_ledger.concern: No admissible evidence shows the material limitation was disclosed, resolved, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: An approved risk acceptance, proof of completed disclosure, or evidence the gap was resolved before certification.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The release policy makes one of those conditions necessary for named launch use cases with material limitations.

concern_ledger.concern: The affected segment is named in two agency grant commitments, and the product materiality note does not address that fact.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Documentation showing the named grant commitments are not covered by the policy, or a formal materiality/risk disposition approved under the policy.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Policy text says low-volume or non-core labels do not resolve materiality when the affected segment is named in commitments.

concern_ledger.concern: The actor relies on general public governance guidance as if it supports this specific certification decision.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Case-specific admissible evidence satisfying the internal release policy, not just general external guidance.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: General guidance does not satisfy the missing internal disclosure and approval predicates required by policy.

decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the affected segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
For named launch use cases, material limitations must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
General external guidance can support process quality but cannot substitute for missing internal policy predicates or approvals.
evidence_requests: Approved risk acceptance covering the grant compliance review gap before launch.
Final legal determination on whether the gap must be disclosed.
Evidence that the required disclosure for the named segment/use case has been completed before certification.
Binding documentation showing the affected grant compliance review segment is not a named launch use case or contractual commitment covered by the policy.
specific_concerns: The record shows the affected segment is named in two agency grant commitments, which makes product 'non-core' framing insufficient under the policy text.

The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, but no disclosure decision, completed disclosure, or approved risk acceptance is in evidence.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.
Public governance guidance on documenting limitations and monitoring risk is general background support, not evidence that this specific certification satisfies the internal release policy.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant on the available record.
That the 5% projected first-month traffic note is enough to negate materiality for the affected segment.
That public model-card or NIST-style guidance materially supports certifying despite the unresolved internal disclosure requirement.
